items.current: **DS pattern now exists** and is the authority for the markup: a 320px rail with a count pill, a hint line, a label-less search field (Input) and either an empty state or a list of AttendeeCards with both booleans off. It is presentational — the tray contents, the count, the search filtering and the drag are all unwired, and the rows are the drag SOURCES the seat rows receive. DERIVED, not a list: the event's people minus everyone seated, recomputed on every change. Role tag + name + company per row, live count badge, predictive search over name AND company, and an empty state for a fully-seated event. Because it derives, the four return paths (unseat, delete table, delete plan, reduce capacity) now put people back BY NAME with no pushing — they used to insert a row labelled by origin ("Table 12 · seat 4") because the occupant's real name was not available. Manually-added guests (342309) survive being unseated because the module remembers anyone it has seen seated who is not on the roster.

items.current: Opens from either Copy Plans button in the header — there are two, one per header section, and both were unwired. ALMOST ENTIRELY THE EVENT PICKER: Figma hand-built this dialog as a copy of the picker, and the pattern already carried every part it needs — modal--lg (768, the same width), the filters search, the list, the ActionCard rows INCLUDING the .event-picker__plans count Figma shows per row, and a footer with [data-ep-count] plus Cancel. So the markup is reused rather than restated, and the dialog carries `data-event-picker` so event-picker.js drives the search, the footer count, Escape, row selection and Cancel. Its event-picker:select / :close are listened for on THIS overlay and the Select-an-event glue is bound to its own, so the two dialogs cannot cross-wire — verified: after copying, the picker still read "6 events · live only". Three deliberate differences from the picker, all drawn: no Live checkbox (hidden in Figma), no group headings (hidden), and no seated progress bar on a row — a seated figure would describe the SOURCE plan, not the destination being chosen. THE SOURCE EVENT IS EXCLUDED so a plan cannot be copied onto the event it came from, and the footer counts DESTINATIONS — five, not six (designer, 2026-09-09). The two frames contradicted each other here: desktop's list starts at Global Payments Forum (5 rows) while mobile lists the source first (6 rows), and BOTH footers say "6 events". Mobile is the picker's "Last used" row surviving with only its group label hidden; the "6" is the un-excluded total. Getting this wrong would have silently doubled every plan onto its own event. Intro copy is data-driven — the plan count and source name are read off the page, so it cannot disagree with the header above it and follows a plan being added or deleted. It reads "1 plan" on this screen where Figma says "2 plans", because this template has one room card; that is the behaviour working, not a mismatch. Choosing a destination bumps that row's plan count BY THE NUMBER COPIED (read, added, rewritten — not incremented by one), toasts what was copied, and closes. Rows carry tabindex, so the whole flow works from the keyboard, which matters because keyboard users cannot drag either. Verified in a browser: pick, place, swap, unseat, cancel and refusal all work by tap and by Enter, and picking does not hijack table selection.

items.element: Seating plans block — .sp-plans in the layout alternatives
items.current: Rebuilt as two rows: the title with New plan and Copy plans to event on one line, the rooms beneath on their own horizontally scrollable line. Desktop gets prev/next ARROWS instead of a scrollbar — hidden until the rooms overflow, and each hides again at its end, so a visible arrow always does something. Touch gets a swipe with no arrow. The room cards KEEP their size-4 (240px) width below 1024 rather than stretching to fill the track, so the cut card at the edge is emergent rather than guaranteed: measured with five plans, a card is cut at 500, 560, 600, 700, 768 and 900px (10% to 97% of a card showing), but at ~527, ~775 and 1023px the cards land exactly flush (track = 248n - 8) and nothing would signal the rest. So a TRAILING FADE is applied whenever the track can still scroll right — a mask driven by the same measurement that hides the next arrow — which does not depend on the arithmetic working out. The data-sp-plans-row hook moved onto the track, so NewPlan.js's chips and DeletePlan.js's 'No plans yet' hint still land in the right place with no change to either module.
items.needs: Nothing server-side. Three implementation notes: the arrow and fade state is re-synced on scroll, on resize, on a mutation of the chip list AND on a timeout after an arrow click, because a smooth scroll fires no scroll events in some environments and a stale arrow is a dead control; the fade uses currentColor as its opaque mask stop, because a mask reads only the alpha channel and hardcoding a colour would breach the token rule; and if the fade is ever dropped, remember the peek is NOT guaranteed at 527, 775 or 1023px with 240px cards.

items.current: The messages, the emphasised names and the Undo button are all hardcoded. The pill is presentational: it owns no show/hide, no auto-dismiss timer and no JS at all — unlike the `Toast` card, it has no close button to wire. `role="status"` (Success) and `role="alert"` (Error) are in place, so a screen reader announces it once it is inserted. WIRED INTO THE DS TEMPLATE 2026-09-09 for table create and edit, from Figma 1:6763 (edited) and 1:6881 (added) in the Seating Planner file. The open question this entry recorded — "who retires a toast" — is now answered: auto-dismiss after 4s (8s when first wired on 2026-09-09, shortened the same day at the designer's request), the timer PAUSES while the pointer is over the pill or focus is inside it so Undo cannot expire mid-read or mid-tab (the WCAG 2.2 concern this entry raised), Esc dismisses, one toast at a time. The host is a fixed, click-through, viewport-centred region 24px off the bottom; only the pill takes pointer events. Both frames place the toast identically (465x58 at x=632 y=1033 in 1728x1117), i.e. centred with a 26px gap — built at --ai-spacing-6 (24px) because 26 maps to no token (designer). Raised via a `sp:toast` CustomEvent, so the raising code needs no load-order guarantee and nothing new lands on `window`. The pill built by JS deliberately omits the `role="status"` the component demo shows: the HOST is the live region, present from load, because a freshly-inserted status element announces unreliably. COPY: both frames emphasise SUBJECT and OBJECT with a plain verb between — "**Table 13** added to **Main Ballroom.**" and "**Table 1** renamed to **Headline Sponsors**". The punctuation differs between them (full stop inside the bold on add, none on rename) and is reproduced as drawn. A third case is not drawn at all — an edit that changes capacity/tier/sponsor/host but not the name — and reads "**Table 2** updated", since "renamed to" would be false there. MEASURED DISCREPANCY, pre-existing and NOT introduced by this wiring: the pill renders 60px tall against Figma's 58. This file's own comment computes 58 as 1+12+32+12+1, assuming a 32px CTA, but `.btn--xs` is 32px of padding+line-height PLUS a 1px border each side, so the CTA is 34 and the pill is 60. Left alone rather than retuning a component signed off on 2026-08-26 from a screen-level task — worth a designer call on whether the CTA or the pill padding should give. DELETE TOAST ADDED 2026-09-09 from Figma 1:43029 desktop / 1:44173 mobile, and it is Type=ERROR rather than success — both frames place `Icon/24px/TriangleAlert` with the --ai-border-error ring where the create and edit toasts place BadgeCheck and the success ring. A removal is reported as a warning. The toast module now takes a `type` in its `sp:toast` detail ('success' | 'error') and picks the modifier and the icon from it, so the two Types the component already had are both in use. Copy keeps the bold-subject / plain-verb / bold-object shape: "**Table 2** has been removed from **Main Ballroom.**", full stop inside the emphasis as with the add toast. Undo restores the card AT ITS ORIGINAL POSITION — the next sibling's id is part of the snapshot, because re-appending would drop a restored table at the end of the grid and table order is how people find them; verified by deleting a middle card and getting the order 1..12 back intact. MOBILE TYPE STEP-DOWN added to the COMPONENT (SeatingToast.css): 13px/16 against the base 14px/20, read off 1:44212 — the file's only mobile toast frame — and confirmed by its get_variable_defs (--ai-font-fixed-2xs 13, --ai-leading-xs 16); the paired desktop toast 1:43089 keeps 14/20, so it is a real breakpoint change. It applies to EVERY toast, not just delete: there is no mobile frame for create or edit, but the step-down is a property of the component at that width rather than of one message, and a delete toast a size smaller than a create toast on the same phone would be the odd outcome. Flagged on that basis. Two positional notes, neither acted on: the delete frames place the toast 44px off the bottom where the create/edit frames use 26px, and the mobile delete frame centres it on the CONTENT COLUMN (x=64 in a 402 frame, right of the 52px sidebar) rather than the viewport — the host uses one viewport-centred 24px offset for all toasts, since three hand-placed offsets across frames read as Figma noise. And the message wraps to two lines on desktop where 1:43089 shows one, because the pill is --ai-size-8 (448) against Figma's unbound 465 — the deviation approved 2026-08-26, whose own comment already says the message is left to wrap deliberately.
items.needs: **Undo is still the part that needs the backend.** It is now WIRED but DOM-only: the toast carries a snapshot of exactly what that one save touched (the card's outerHTML, the plan totals, the seat panel and the selection) and restores it. That is honest for a front-end prototype and is reversal of *that specific* operation rather than "undo the last change" — but it is DOM state, not data, and dies on reload. this screen only needs to consume the selection. **`seating-planner:event-chosen` is the seam**: its `{ id, name }` should load the planner into the same `.seating-screen` card and persist the choice. **Open (design):** there is no scrim token in the scale (both themes are raw rgba), and the dark-mode scrim density is likely system-wide rather than specific to this screen. **Which state renders is the plan COUNT, not the click** — an event that already has plans must go straight to the planner, not to No Plan, so the front end needs the plan list (or at least its length) with the event; see `seating-room-list`. **New Plan** in the header is what leaves this state — see `seating-new-plan` for what it must create (a plan generates its tables, per the empty state's own copy). **The SeatingHeader's event details** should come from the chosen event rather than its hardcoded copy, which is the same data `seating-header` already specs. **`seating-planner:plan-created` is the create-plan seam** — see `seating-new-plan`: creating a plan must generate its tables from the tables/seats/shape values, which is exactly what the empty state's own copy promises. **Validation must move server-side**: the 6-12 seats rule and the required-name rule are currently transcribed from Figma copy into the front end, so the server has to enforce them and should return the messages (cf. `seating-capacity-reduction`). **Open (design):** two help strings do not exist in any frame (Plan name and Seats/table are masked by errors in the only help-on frame), and Tables' help reads like validation but is styled as a hint.
